newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Amplats shines as merger talks on track.
newsitem.headline: Amplats shines as merger talks on track.

text.p: Shares in South Africa's Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd (Amplats), the world's largest platinum producer, rose on Wednesday on news that the restructuring of the group was proceeding well.
"(The rise) is on the cautionary this morning. The restructuring is seen as a favourable move," a dealer said.

Amplats said earlier talks on the merger of the four group firms, Amplats, Rustenburg Platinum Holdings Ltd (Rusplats), Lebowa Platinum Mines Ltd (Leplats), Potgietersrust Platinums Ltd (PP Rust), into one, were proceeding well.
By 1220 GMT Amplats' shares were up 105 cents or 3.5 percent to 30.75 rand on volume of 127,100.
Rusplats gained 50 cents to 73.25 rand, Leplats was up eight cents at 290 cents but PP Rust dipped 50 cents to 26.50 rand.
Amplats said last month the merger supported the group's strategy of moving its operations down the cost curve and increasing operational flexibility to take full advantage of market conditions.
The merger, together with the development of a new mine at BoschkoppiE and expansion of PP Rust's concentrator, would enhance Amplats' position as the world leader in platinum.
Dealers said a stronger platinum price on Wednesday, which fixed $2.50 firmer at $396.00/397.00 in London, was also propping up related shares.
